newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia orders Norilsk sale suspended - Interfax.
newsitem.headline: Russia orders Norilsk sale suspended - Interfax.

text.p: Russia's Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin has ordered the tender for 38 percent of Norilsk Nickel , the winner of which was due to be announced on Tuesday, to be suspended, Interfax news agency said Monday.

"Chernomyrdin has instructed the Russian State Property Committee (Russia's privatisation ministry) and the Federal Property Fund to urgently postpone the tender of 38 percent of RAO Norilsky Nikel, scheduled to take place on August 5," Interfax said, quoting unnamed government sources.
Uneximbank, which controlled the stake and is taking part in the tender, and the Federal Property Fund, could not confirm the report.
State Property Fund Chairman Igor Lipkin said that if Chernomyrdin were to make such an instruction, then the fund would suspend the sale.

Uneximbank announced it was putting up for sale the 38 percent stake in the base and precious metals mining giant early last month. It won the right to manage the stake, which represents 51 percent of voting shares in the company, in a shares-for-loans scheme in 1995.

But the sale has been dogged by controversy after potential bidders in the tender complained the terms of the sale were unfair, and gave undue advantage to Uneximbank, which analysts had widely tipped to win the stake.

Public uproar over Uneximbank's apparent advantage in the Norilsk tender has grown since a consortium led by Uneximbank won 25 percent plus one share of Russian telecommunications holding company Svyazinvest for $1.875 billion.
